# m.forex.last_quote

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The latest best bid and ask of each currency pair.

Call it from a session `m`, made with `dm.MassiveSession()`:

```python
m.forex.last_quote(symbols)
```

- [Query methods](README.md#query-methods): `fetch()`, `poll(interval)`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol`
- `poll(interval, mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND)`: appends each new state of a row, identified by `Symbol` and `Timestamp`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows the [shared rules](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Currency pairs as Massive's tickers, such as `C:EURUSD`. `dm.ALL` is refused: use `m.forex.snapshots(dm.ALL)`. |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Last Quote (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Currencies Basic | Not included |
| Currencies Starter | Real-time |
| Currencies Business | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The row's instrument, as Massive's ticker. From REST: the request's `from` parameter. |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the UTC date of `Timestamp`. |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's event time. From REST `timestamp`: "The Unix millisecond timestamp." |
| `BidPrice` | double | The bid price. |
| `AskPrice` | double | The ask price. |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/forex/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, by the local clock. Rows that arrive together, in one REST page, share it. It isn't Massive's time, and it isn't monotonic. In a `poll()` table, it's the time of the poll the row's values came from. |
